findings.quote: Water moves both ways at the same rate, so the solute amounts are equal.
findings.problem: This is wrong as stated. A cell in an isotonic solution has the same solute concentration as the solution, not the same amount of solute: a beaker holds far more solute than one red blood cell. The lesson defines concentration, then drops it where it matters. The same looseness is in "**Isotonic** solution: equal solute inside and out." and "**Hypotonic** solution: less solute outside than inside the cell." The base lesson compared concentrations.
findings.source: OpenStax Biology 2e, 5.2 Passive Transport, https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/5-2-passive-transport (isotonic means the same osmolarity, which is total solute concentration); base revision 7032eec5

findings.quote: Some cells keep their DNA in a **nucleus**.
findings.problem: This paragraph has four sentences; the limit is three. Three others also have four: "A **solute** is a substance", "**Diffusion** is the net movement" and "**Active transport** moves a substance". Round 1 named this rule, and three of these paragraphs are still over the limit.
